question: Which of the following metals exists in liquid state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mercury**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Metals are the elements which have lustre, are good conductors of heat and electricity, are malleable and ductile.
 
• All metals exist in a solid-state at room temperature.
 
• Mercury is the only metal which exists in the liquid state at room temperature.
 
• Mercury:
 
 
• The chemical symbol for mercury is 'Hg' and its atomic number 80.
 
• It is a shiny, silvery liquid metal at room temperature.
 
• Mercury is used in thermometers because of its proportional expansion or compression with a change in temperature.
 
• It is also used in fluorescent lamps, Batteries and barometers.
 
• Mercury consumption for living beings is toxic (Minamata disease is related to mercury intoxication).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Solid State: If an object has a fixed shape and volume we can say it is solid.
 
 
• The inter-molecular force between them is strong and usually in a regular pattern.
 
• Most of the metals are solid at room temperatures except – Mercury (Hg) melting point – (-38.83° C).
 
• Non-metals are also solid at room temperature except- Bromine (Br) melting point – (-7.2° C)
 
 

 
• Liquid State: When an object has fixed volume but no shape we can say it is in the form of liquid.
 
 
• Their intermolecular force is not as strong as solid, they can flow freely.
 
• They are very little compressible.
 
 

 
• Gaseous State: In this state molecules can move freely and the inter-molecular force are very low. It has no shape and size. It is in a gaseous state.
 
 
• They are very compressible.
